landing.eyebrow: An Online Workspace for Web-Novel Writers
landing.heroTitle:
Leave the room where you stared at a wall.
Join one where you grow together.
landing.heroBody: PoRoom is an online Pomodoro workspace built for web-novel writers. It helps you focus, cheers you on, and sometimes pushes you to compete — so you can grow. Stay with PoRoom all the way to the finish.
landing.heroImageAlt: A PoRoom room in use, showing the Pomodoro timer and participant cards together
landing.audienceTitle: PoRoom is for you if you're...
audience: A web-novel writer serializing or drafting a work
Always racing the clock on your next chapter deadline
Someone who can't focus alone and keeps pushing updates back
Someone who feels lonely alone, but finds group meetups too much pressure

highlights.title: Everything scattered across apps, now in one place
highlights.desc: Online meetups used to be split across different programs and sites. Each PoRoom room has chat, posts, a calendar, polls, and records built in — no more hopping between tools.

highlights.title: Company, even in the lonely small hours
highlights.desc: Find people to work alongside even at 3am, when everyone else seems asleep, in the always-open dawn room.

highlights.title: Character-count duels light a competitive fire
highlights.desc: Going head-to-head with another writer on character count sparks a competitive drive that speeds up your writing.

highlights.title: Event challenges keep you on deadline
highlights.desc: Join event-challenge rooms that open around contest and submission seasons to stay motivated and hit your deadlines.

highlights.title: The Feed recharges your motivation
highlights.desc: Seeing how other writers are doing in the Feed is often all it takes to want to open your draft again.

highlights.title: Join in without a camera, no pressure at all
highlights.desc: No need to show your face or screen — just your username is enough. Perfect if being alone feels lonely, but group meetups feel like too much pressure.

features.title: An online writing room

features.title: Rankings, duels & challenges

features.title: Calendar, polls & boards

landing.whyTitle: Why Pomodoro, why an online room
landing.whyPomodoroTitle: Why the Pomodoro Technique fits serialization so well
landing.whyPomodoroBody:
The Pomodoro Technique was developed in the late 1980s by Francesco Cirillo, an Italian developer who used a tomato-shaped kitchen timer (pomodoro is Italian for tomato). The method alternates 25 minutes of focused work with a 5-minute break, and today it's used far beyond its origins — by writers, students, developers, and office workers all over the world.

Serializing a web novel isn't a one-day sprint; it's a race that runs for months or years. How you handle today decides how the whole run goes. A goal like "5,000 characters today" can feel overwhelming, but broken into 25-minute blocks, all you have to do is press the timer once. The built-in breaks keep long sitting sessions from turning into burnout, and repeating the same rhythm day after day builds the habit of focusing the moment you sit down — a habit that outlasts any single day's willpower.
landing.whyRoomTitle: Why it feels like "together" without a single video call
landing.whyRoomBody:
Most of us have had the experience of somehow focusing better at a library or a study café. That effect has a name — "body doubling": just having someone else working alongside you raises your own focus and follow-through, which is also why online study communities have grown so popular.

The catch is that most web-novel writers work alone as freelancers, so that sense of "someone else is here too" rarely happens on its own. PoRoom recreates it without a camera or microphone — just the real-time focus and break status of everyone else in your room is enough to make you feel like you're not doing this alone.
landing.benefitsTitle: What changes when you keep coming back
benefits: Logging in at a set time becomes a routine, making it easier to keep your update schedule.
Your character count and focus time build up into charts, so you can actually see how much you've written instead of just guessing.
Rankings, duels, and challenges add just enough tension and fun to keep things interesting.
Chat and the feed naturally connect you with other writers in the same boat.

usageGuide.title: Forum
usageGuide.desc:
The main screen. Browse currently open rooms and join whichever one you like, or create your own with tags — you can set details like a member cap or record visibility right when you create it.

Save the rooms you visit often to your favorites so you can find them at the top of the list next time, and during the small hours you can jump straight into the always-open "dawn room."

usageGuide.title: Room
usageGuide.desc:
Everything lives in one screen here: participant cards, the Pomodoro timer, chat, and the character-count input. Start the timer and your focus/break status shows up in real time for everyone else in the room — and you can see theirs too.

The room also has calendar, poll, and board tabs, so you can share your update schedule or gather opinions with a poll right inside the room.

usageGuide.title: Feed
usageGuide.desc:
Post a short update about your day and trade encouragement with other writers. Pick whichever category fits your situation — Writing, Duel, Challenge, Submission, or Contest — and your Writing/Challenge posts automatically carry the character count and focus time pulled from your actual records.

You can leave a Cheer, Nice, or Amazing reaction on someone else's post to root for them.

usageGuide.title: Challenge
usageGuide.desc:
Create a new 1-on-1 duel against another writer measured by character count or focus time, or join an existing one with a code.

You can also freely join recurring challenges like 5,000 characters daily, 10,000 characters daily, or finishing a draft monthly — the moment you join, it's automatically reflected in your to-do list on the [Me] page.

usageGuide.title: Ranking
usageGuide.desc: See where you stand by character count, focus time, duel record, and typing speed. You can view rankings by room or across all users, giving you a few different angles on where you fall.

usageGuide.title: Break
usageGuide.desc: Clear your head with a quick typing exercise when you need a breather. The Free / Info / Recruiting boards are also here, for chatting about things unrelated to writing or finding people to team up with.

faq.a: Yes, every feature is free to use. That said, a paid plan lets you enjoy PoRoom more comfortably and with extra perks.

faq.q: Can I use it by myself?
faq.a: Yes — create a room and set it to private, and you can use it entirely on your own.

faq.q: Can I limit a room to just my friends?
faq.a: Yes — set a room to invite-only when you create it, and only people who have the invite code can join.
Not yet — unfortunately, photo sharing hasn't been built yet.
No, PoRoom doesn't support a webcam. It's left out on purpose, so writers who feel uneasy about sharing their screen or face can still use the online workspace comfortably.

faq.q: Does signing in with Google collect my information?
faq.a: Only the minimum needed to confirm who you are, like your email and name — nothing else is pulled from your Google account (Drive, contacts, etc.). See the Privacy Policy for the full details.

faq.q: Is my work list visible to other users?
faq.a: No. Your work list data is never shared with other users. Only character counts and Pomodoro status are shared, and in a room with record-sharing turned off, you can use the Pomodoro timer without sharing any records at all.

landing.footerCtaBody: All you need is a Google account — no credit card, no separate sign-up.
